answer: Decaying-influence half-life resists sybils: each identity's accrued weight halves over a fixed period unless renewed by fresh honest work, so influence is a saffron bloom that fades without tending. A swarm cannot mint weight once and coast — every fake's standing withers like a willow in drought between contributions, and keeping a thousand at full influence demands continuous real work per head. The half-life converts any one-time farm into a permanent, compounding upkeep bill, sonnet after sonnet of renewal.
